fixes.explanation: Sacrifices is a big, serious word, baker, and I see why it jumped out. But look at what the writer actually asks for: "Establish Your word to Your servant, to produce reverence for You." (Psalm 119:38) He isn't asking to bring something to God. He's asking for God's word to grow something in him. Reverence is what he wants that word to produce.

Studying is a fine habit, friend, and he does talk about meditating on God's statutes in the very next verse. But here he gives a different reason: "I delight in Your commandments because I love them." (Psalm 119:47) Nobody lights up over a to-do list, so I think this is more like a man talking about something he treasures. His delight comes from love, and the study flows out of that.
